propositions: `rebar comment <id> --body-file <path>` stores the literal flag token as the comment body and exits 0, discarding intended content.
The failure is undetectable: exit 0, no stderr, and a comment appears so a length check passes while the content is lost.
The footgun has affected two independent sessions, losing their durable ticket-store records.
A body argument beginning with `-` should be rejected with a non-zero exit naming the correct form, with a `--` escape hatch for legitimate dash-leading bodies.
The same guard should cover all positional-body commands (comment, create, edit, session-log), with tests asserting rejection of `--body-file` and `--body` forms.
Consider adding a real `--body-file` option since two sessions reached for it and positional args are awkward for large markdown bodies.
